title: Geometric irreducibility detected by the generic residue field
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $X$ an irreducible $k$-scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-irreducible-components]. Let $\xi$ be its generic point, meaning $\overline{\{\xi\}}=|X|$ [def-sc-generic-point], and give its residue field $\kappa(\xi)$ [def-weil-residue-field] the induced $k$-algebra structure. Then $X$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$ if and only if $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. No reducedness or finite-type hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For an open surjective morphism p:Z→X and generic point ξ of X, Z is irreducible if and only if its scheme-theoretic fibre at ξ is irreducible. Forward: the generic point z of Z maps to ξ because continuous surjective maps take a generic point to a generic point. Every nonempty open of Z contains z, hence any two opens meeting the fibre meet there at z. Reverse: apply Mathlib IsPreirreducible.preimage_of_dense_isPreirreducible_fiber to the open map p and the dense singleton {ξ}. The nonempty fibre supplies nonemptiness of Z. Mathlib Scheme.Hom.fiberHomeo identifies the fibre with the topological preimage of {ξ}.

For every field K and morphism y:Spec K→Spec k, y is surjective and universally open. Thus the projection p:X×_k Spec K→X is open and surjective, by Mathlib base-change instances (UniversallyOpen for an integral singleton target). Apply step 1. Pullback symmetry followed by pullbackRightPullbackFstIso identifies p.fiber ξ with Spec κ(ξ)×_k Spec K. Therefore these two base changes are irreducible simultaneously. Quantifying over K and y is exactly geometric irreducibility of the two structure morphisms.
